hook: Textbooks said your gut's inner surface is the size of a tennis court.
twist: A 2014 measurement found about 32 square metres: half a badminton court. Along the way: the stomach churns for hours, the liver sends up to 800 ml of bile a day, the small intestine's folds and villi do the absorbing, and the bacteria eat the leftovers.
angle: A relay race through the cast, each organ handing the lunch on, ending on the corrected number. Big number: 30 square metres.
why_now: Scout: food-in-your-body Shorts (banana digestion) top 103M, median of top 25 7.0M: the strongest body topic.
risks: Surface area figures: 30 m² (Wikipedia, small intestine) vs about 32 m² (whole tract, Helander & Fändriks 2014). Say 'about thirty'.
